definitions.meaning: ... as in commonly known or recognised
a witch's attendant spirit, often in animal form

explanation.definitionFit: Something often seen is familiar, and a witch's demon companion, such as a black cat, is called her familiar.

clue.text: First flag on lofty new building's a swastika

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of flag is used
a new building assembles the letters of lofty in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A swastika flag flies above a tall new building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes F from 'flag'; 'new building's' rebuilds LOFTY as YLFOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fylfot is a heraldic and old decorative name for the hooked cross.

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of animal go mad

explanation.surface: A box of animal crackers is greeted as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal crackers' looks like the biscuits; 'crackers' is the anagram signal, and 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines.

indicators.note: afflicted suggests the letters are troubled and thrown out of order

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital suffers badly from staff indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a sluggish lack of energy or interest, close to listlessness.

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means gets rid of or cuts

explanation.definitionFit: To cut staff is to sack them, and the same word is the plural of the woodcutter's blade.

clue.text: Mark and Jack find a beetle

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a jack is a sailor, and so is an AB, an able seaman

explanation.surface: Two men named Mark and Jack come across a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and Jack look like two names; Jack is the sailor, AB (able seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Conservationists want to protect an old ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep ravine with steep sides, a large-scale gorge.

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of puritans are jumbled

explanation.surface: Puritans are baffled by a menacing Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the mystic who held malign sway over the last Tsar's court.

indicators.note: donned means put on, so the colour is put on after the emblem

parts.note: insignia means a badge or emblem
cardinal red is the scarlet of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A cardinal puts on his insignia when hurried along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests the churchman but gives the colour RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgered means harassed or pestered persistently, nagged into action.

indicators.note: after places the anagram before the word meaning after this, read in answer order
wild suggests the letters of glen run riot into a new order

parts.note: after this means then, next in time

explanation.surface: Someone finds a wild glen and then a stretch of land beyond it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns GLEN into LENG; 'after this' gives THEN, which follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to make it longer, extending it out.

definitions.meaning: new and never put to use

explanation.definitionFit: Being unaccustomed to a thing and a brand-new item never handled both share the sense of not having been used.

clue.text: Willing to take bike out in this kind of weather?

definitions.text: Willing to take bike out in this kind of weather?

parts.words: Willing to take bike out in this kind of weather?
parts.note: someone keen to keep riding, saying cycle on, even in a violent storm

explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating storm is the weather; the clue plays on cycling on regardless.

clue.text: Deployed to ensure a smooth run?

definitions.text: Deployed to ensure a smooth run?

parts.words: Deployed to ensure a smooth run?
parts.note: a lubricating can squirted onto machinery so that it runs smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: A small can with a spout lubricates moving parts so machinery runs without friction.

clue.text: Little Bear is centre of attention

definitions.meaning: the constellation Ursa Minor, whose name in Greek means dog's tail and holds the Pole Star
a focus of admiration everyone looks at

explanation.definitionFit: The constellation guiding sailors became a byword for anything that draws all eyes, a focal point of admiration.

indicators.note: spoken of tells us the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man, followed by the contraction I'd

explanation.surface: A Scotsman admits he would have talked about being rich.
explanation.walkthrough: MON, Scots for 'man', plus I'D said together sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellheeled means wealthy, and being rich is having plenty of cash.

parts.note: G is a musical note
a peer is a noble, a member of the aristocracy

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain lord has gone to the bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble describes base, dishonourable behaviour, the conduct of someone morally debased.

clue.text: Yield to pressure and be generous?

definitions.meaning: to bend or collapse under strain

explanation.definitionFit: A rope or floor that bends under weight is said to sag that way, and a donor hands things over freely.

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of put deals are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was thrilled to cancel some deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulsated means throbbed or quivered, as a heart does with excitement.

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of crow and lady are prepared in a new form

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the crow a woman cooked is in fact chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CROW and LADY; 'chicken' suggests poultry but means scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for timid, lacking courage.

clue.text: Going round the castle have light snack, with a mineral

indicators.note: going round means the snack word wraps round the chess piece

parts.note: a bite is a light snack
in chess the castle is also called the rook

explanation.surface: Visitors walk round the castle, have a snack, then look at a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' is the chess piece ROOK, placed inside BITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brookite is a mineral form of titanium dioxide.

clue.text: A group on foot? Characters in the middle are mounted

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit in the middle of the words group on

explanation.surface: A band of people travelling on foot; the middle ones are on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A group on foot?' seems to invite a word for infantry, but the letters are inside 'group on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mounted means being set on top of something, as a rider sits on a horse.

clue.text: Girl getting another girl to sign

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl persuades a friend to sign a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb (to sign) but is the star sign LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonora is a female first name, as in Beethoven's heroine.
Work by hand is described with the Latin word for hand, and a handbook of directions bears the same name.

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: coarse means rough

explanation.surface: A stretch of sea is said to be choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the sea, but means a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is the channel a river or stream runs in.

indicators.note: ahead puts the pot-hole word in front of the other piece

parts.note: a pot-hole is a deep cave
at can mean against, as in hurling oneself at a door

explanation.surface: A sign warns walkers of a pothole in the road ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot-hole' suggests a hole in a road, but is the caver's vertical cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso, Latin for let him beware.

parts.note: the main is the open ocean, and its highways are routes ships follow

explanation.definitionFit: Shipping routes across the ocean are the marine equivalent of roads.

clue.text: Extinct creature scholar brought to capital

parts.note: the dodo is the famous extinct flightless bird
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar carries a dodo specimen to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodoma is the capital city of Tanzania.

clue.text: Little dog seen to stretch out, on the quiet

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to eke out is to stretch out a supply

explanation.surface: A small dog is spotted stretching quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical mark for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is short for Pekingese, a small lapdog.

clue.text: Monotony of new diet Mothers' Union rejected

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of diet are made over in another order
rejected means thrown back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MU stands for the Mothers' Union, a Christian charity

explanation.surface: A women's group turns down a fresh diet as boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes TEDI from DIET; 'rejected' turns MU into UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is wearisome sameness, the dullness of a routine that never varies.

clue.text: Descent from tricky ridge -— not right to peer around

indicators.note: to peer around means the shortened word wraps round the other piece
not right says the letter R, for right, is dropped
tricky suggests the letters of ridge are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Coming down a treacherous ridge, a climber must not peer round to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes R from PEER, leaving PEE; 'tricky' makes DIGRE from RIDGE, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree means ancestry or lineage, one's line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Thirsty insect? Angler knows it's a fake

parts.note: dry means thirsty
a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A fisherman recognises that his lure is an artificial bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly fishermen use artificial lures that float on the surface, imitating real flies.

clue.text: Building for the people, in principle

indicators.note: in puts the people inside the word for principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or doctrine
men means people

explanation.surface: A building designed for ordinary people, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as 'theoretically', but 'in' places MEN inside TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, often for poorer tenants.
